summary: Full E2E + API validation for iteration 45 P2 items: (1) SAFE REFACTOR — onboarding endpoints in routers/onboarding.py + OsEditor.js/OsReady.js, (2) ENFORCED TASK-LEVEL APPROVAL (submit→review→approve/reject with 403 for non-approvers), (3) SMART ASSIGNMENT (role → least-loaded member). Backend pytest 9/9 PASS, Frontend Playwright covers onboarding regression, approval happy + reject, and smart-assign visibility on Board view. Everything works as spec'd.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 4056 lines. Iteration 44 already flagged this — the onboarding refactor helps but tasks (create/patch/approve/reject/updates/prioritize/execution-plan), auth, decisions, workflows, dashboard should each get their own routers file to bring server.py < 700 lines per file.

The approval-rejection prompt uses window.prompt (native browser prompt) which is jarring and can't be styled/tested cleanly. Consider replacing with a small shadcn Dialog (data-testid='reject-reason-input' + 'reject-confirm-button') for both UX consistency and reliable Playwright testing.

Dev console still emits 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>' hydration warnings (from x-source instrumentation wrapping option children). Non-blocking in production build, pollutes dev console. Same finding as iteration 43.

PATCH /api/tasks/{id} enforces the approval gate silently — an assignee who wants to complete an approval-required task will see status flip to 'review' with no user-facing hint in the current PATCH response (only the notification to the approver). Consider returning a small 'submitted_for_approval: true' flag in the response so the frontend can toast confirmation deterministically (currently the FE recovers via cache refresh).

_can_approve_task(user, t) treats every 'owner' as an approver even for tasks with a specific approver_id assigned to someone else. This matches the requirement ('owner can always override') but on a bigger team an owner accidentally approving another approver's queue could be surprising. Consider distinguishing 'owner-override' as a separate action so audit log shows it.

No GET /api/tasks/{id} endpoint exists — clients have to fetch the full list and filter. Consider adding it for cleaner single-task refreshes after approve/reject (tests worked around by using PATCH response).

pick_least_loaded_member is called on create + on operational patch. Good. But there's no fallback message when a role has NO members — the task will silently be created with assignee_id=None (behavior confirmed OK for 'no member of role X exists'), but a UI hint would help (e.g. 'No sales member — task left unassigned').

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 45 fully validated all 3 P2 items. Backend: /api/tasks/{id}/approve and /reject enforce _can_approve_task (owner OR approver_id), PATCH /api/tasks/{id} status=done on approval_required tasks flips to review+pending. Smart assignment via pick_least_loaded_member works for role='sales' -> Priya Nair and role='production' -> Amit Verma (or whoever is least loaded). Onboarding refactor: /api/onboarding/suggest, /api/onboarding/os-blueprint, PATCH /api/tenant/os-blueprint all 200. Frontend selectors verified: complete-<id> button relabels to 'Submit for approval' when approval_required is set; approval-actions-<id> block appears in Under Review with approve-<id> + reject-<id> children; op-approval-<id> badge shows Pending approval / Approved / Changes requested. Reject uses native window.prompt for the reason. Smart-assign via task-role-select works; Board view exposes task-assignee-<id> testid; MyWork only shows tasks assigned to the current user so smart-assigned tasks won't appear in the owner's MyWork unless they're the least-loaded member of that role.
